target: native x86-64, 13th Gen Intel Core i5-13400F (16 threads), dev desktop
purpose: Pre-optimization baseline for vector search — the reference a later vector optimization (signature-tier layout: signatures resident + int8 in mmap; or a binary HNSW traversal) is measured against. Rerun both after the change; the delta on the SAME machine is what matters (absolute numbers are machine-dependent).

matrix.note: fill < 24k is searched flat, fill >= 24k through the HNSW graph maintain builds

speed_us_per_query.metric: Criterion median wall time per recall, microseconds
speed_us_per_query.observations: flat scales linearly with fill; HNSW is sub-linear (60k faster than flat-20k despite 3x the data); dimension roughly doubles cost.

maintain_graph_build_s.metric: one-time HNSW build during maintain, seconds (a maintain cost, not a query cost)

recall_quality.metric: recall@8 vs exact brute-force cosine over the ORIGINAL f32 vectors (ground truth testgen still holds), self-excluded, averaged over 100 evenly-sampled queries; min is the worst single query
recall_quality.isolation: w_recency=0 and a vector-only query, so the fused ranking collapses to the pure vector top-k — recall reflects quantization + HNSW alone, not recency re-ranking
recall_quality.interpretation: Recall is bounded by the CURRENT design, not a harness bug. Even 'flat' is two-phase: a 1-bit sign-signature Hamming prefilter keeps only the best max(4k,64)=64 candidates, which are then int8-rescored — so a true f32 neighbour missed by the coarse signature is never rescored. The fixed 64-candidate sieve is why flat recall falls as fill grows (64/2000 vs 64/20000). HNSW adds graph-approximation loss on top; min=0.000 is a worst-case query where signature+graph missed all 8. NOTE: these are SYNTHETIC testgen vectors (random) — their nearest neighbours are near-arbitrary, so this understates real quality. See real_embeddings below.

real_embeddings_ollama.corpus: 2000 meaningful English sentences (topic templates x fillers), flat regime, recall@8 vs exact f32 cosine over 200 sampled queries, self-excluded, w_recency=0

sweep_by_query_k.note: query k widens the sieve (max(4k,64)) AND the returned window; recall@8 = true top-8 found anywhere in the returned top-k

real_embeddings_ollama.conclusion: On REAL embeddings there is no quality problem. recall@8 hits 1.000 (even worst-case) at k=16 — the true 8 neighbours ARE found; the default k=8 output window just clips ones int8 quantization nudged to ranks 9-16. IMPORTANT (corrected): the internal candidate margin is NOT the lever — the vector source already fetches SOURCE_CAP=128 candidates (rescore sieve up to 512) into the fusion; recall.rs:58/291. The 0.867 at k=8 is int8 ranking precision at the top-8 boundary, not a narrow sieve. The only lever is the final output window k, which is caller-controlled query semantics: an app wanting exact top-N asks for k=2N and takes the first N (free — speed is flat across k, ~124 us, the O(n) signature pass dominates). No engine change, and no signature-tier / binary-traversal / format change, is warranted by recall at this scale. The synthetic baseline was pessimistic (random vectors).
